evals.prompt: I want to add a notifications feature to my app. Users should see a list of notifications on the :app and a summary on their Wear OS watch. Scaffold the feature and set up the basic structure.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/generate.sh feature notifications --wear, creates correct module structure with platform submodules, follows naming conventions

assertions.text: Uses scripts/generate.sh feature notifications --wear (not manual file creation) to generate the feature
Passes the --wear flag since the feature targets both :app and :wear
Feature is created under features/notifications/ with both app/ and wear/ submodules
Does not create a flat feature module (no features/notifications/src/ without platform submodules)
Mentions registering Koin DI modules in the platform shells' AppModule.kt / WearAppModule.kt as a follow-up step
Mentions adding navigation routes in the platform shell modules as a follow-up step
Mentions adding strings in :core:strings (not in :core or :core:data)
Does not add dependencies between feature modules
Feature deps in build.gradle.kts are :core:domain + :core:strings only (NOT :core:data)

evals.prompt: I need a use case that fetches the user's workout history from the repository and returns it sorted by date. Create the GetWorkoutHistory use case.
evals.expected_output: Writes the use case file directly (no script — scaffold-usecase.sh has been retired), places it in :core:domain, follows the documented pattern with kotlin.Result<T>, wires DI in coreDataModule

assertions.text: Writes the use case file directly (does NOT reference scaffold-usecase.sh — it has been retired)
Use case is placed in :core:domain (core/domain/src/main/kotlin/<package>/domain/usecase/), not in :core:data or a feature module
Use case package is com.<base>.domain.usecase (no repeated 'core' segment)
Use case returns kotlin.Result<T> (built-in, not a custom wrapper type)
Use case takes a repository as a constructor parameter (dependency injection)
Mentions registering the use case in coreDataModule (in :core:data) with factory { GetWorkoutHistoryUseCase(get()) }
Does not put business logic in a feature module
Mentions writing a test for the use case (red-green TDD)

evals.prompt: I have a data class called WorkoutSummary that's used by both the :features:dashboard and :features:profile features. Right now it's in features/dashboard/app/. Where should I move it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends moving to :core:domain (specifically core/domain/.../domain/model/), explains features can't depend on each other, only on :core:domain

assertions.text: Recommends moving WorkoutSummary to :core:domain (specifically core/domain/.../domain/model/)
Explains that feature modules cannot depend on each other — only on :core:domain (and :core:strings)
Does not suggest adding a dependency between :features:dashboard and :features:profile
Does not suggest creating a new shared module between features (the answer is :core:domain)
Mentions that Gradle enforces this compile-time boundary

evals.prompt: We already have a :features:dashboard:app module for :app. I want to add watch support so users can see their dashboard on Wear OS too. Walk me through what I need to do.
evals.expected_output: Creates wear/ submodule alongside app/, uses Wear Material 3, separate ViewModel, wires in :wear platform shell

assertions.text: Creates a wear/ submodule alongside the existing app/ submodule (features/dashboard/wear/)
Wear submodule gets its own ViewModel (e.g., WearDashboardViewModel), not sharing the :app ViewModel
Uses Wear Material 3 components (androidx.wear.compose.material3), not regular Material 3
Creates a Wear-specific Koin DI module for the feature
Mentions wiring navigation in the :wear platform shell (not in the feature module)
States that business logic in :core:domain is already shared — no changes needed there
Does not suggest sharing UI or ViewModels between app/ and wear/ submodules
Wear feature module depends on :core:domain + :core:strings only (NOT :core:data)

evals.prompt: I want to add a home screen widget that shows today's step count. Set it up for me.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/generate.sh widget to create the :widget module at root level. Depends on :core:data + :core:strings, uses Glance, does not put code in :app

assertions.text: Uses scripts/generate.sh widget to scaffold the module (not manual file creation)
Creates a :widget module at root level (widget/), not inside :app or a feature module
Widget module depends on :core:data and :core:strings, not on :app, :wear, or any feature module
Uses Glance (Compose-based) for the widget implementation
Accesses step count data through a use case or repository from :core (wired via :core:data)
Does not put widget code inside the :app module

evals.prompt: I need a new settings feature — just for the :app, no watch support needed. Users can toggle dark mode and change their language. Set up the feature module.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/generate.sh feature settings (no --wear flag), still creates app/ submodule (not flat), adds strings in :core:strings

assertions.text: Uses scripts/generate.sh feature settings without the --wear flag (:app-only feature)
Creates features/settings/app/ submodule, NOT a flat features/settings/src/ structure
Does NOT create a features/settings/wear/ submodule since Wear support was not requested
Uses Koin for DI (not Hilt/Dagger)
Uses StateFlow in the ViewModel (not LiveData)
Adds strings to :core:strings/src/main/res/values/strings.xml (not in the feature module's own resources)
Mentions that adding Wear support later is just running scripts/generate.sh feature settings --wear after deleting the existing feature

evals.prompt: We built :features:feed as an :app-only feature. Now I want the feed on Wear OS too. Walk me through the full plan — what needs to move, what stays, and what's new.
evals.expected_output: Creates wear/ submodule with separate ViewModel using Wear Material 3, keeps :core:domain logic untouched, strings already in :core:strings (no migration needed)

assertions.text: Creates features/feed/wear/ submodule alongside existing features/feed/app/
Wear submodule gets its own ViewModel (not sharing the :app ViewModel)
Uses Wear Material 3 components, not regular Material 3
States that business logic in :core:domain does not need changes
Does NOT suggest moving strings from feature to :core — strings already live centrally in :core:strings, no migration needed
Does not suggest sharing ViewModels or UI between app/ and wear/

evals.prompt: I'm fetching articles from the API and caching them in Room. Should this caching logic live in the use case (GetArticlesUseCase) or in the repository (ArticleRepositoryImpl)? Also, after fetching I need to filter out articles the user has already read — where does that filtering go?
evals.expected_output: Caching in repository (data layer concern in :core:data), filtering read articles in use case (business rule in :core:domain). Explains the boundary between data and domain layers.

assertions.text: Places caching logic (fetch from API + store in Room) in the repository (in :core:data), not in the use case
Places the 'filter out read articles' logic in the use case (in :core:domain), not in the repository
Explains why: caching is a data-layer concern (how data is stored/retrieved), while filtering by read-status is a business rule (what data the user should see)
Notes that the repository interface lives in :core:domain and the implementation in :core:data
Repository method signature returns raw data without business filtering applied
Use case follows the project pattern: suspend operator fun invoke() returning kotlin.Result<T> (not a custom wrapper type)

evals.prompt: I need to add a Wear OS complication that shows today's step count on the user's watch face. How should I set this up?
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/generate.sh complications. Module depends only on :core:domain. Uses SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/generate.sh complications to scaffold the module
Creates :complications module at root level (complications/), not inside :wear or a feature module
Complications module depends only on :core:domain, not on :wear, :app, :core:data, or any feature module
Uses SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService to serve complication data
Accesses step count data through a use case from :core:domain
Does not put complication code inside the :wear module
Explains that complications are standalone OS entry points the watch face calls directly, outside the app's UI

evals.prompt: Start a brand new project called fasting with package com.charliesbot.fasting that targets both phone and Wear OS. Set up the project from scratch.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/init.sh, then scripts/generate.sh app and scripts/generate.sh wear. Does not invoke generate.sh with multi-flag syntax.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/init.sh fasting com.charliesbot.fasting first
After init, cd's into the project directory before running generate
Runs scripts/generate.sh app to add the :app module
Runs scripts/generate.sh wear to add the :wear module
Does NOT pass the package as an argument to generate.sh (it reads from gradle.properties)
Mentions that init.sh creates :core:domain, :core:data, :core:strings automatically
Does NOT manually create build.gradle.kts files for any module

evals.prompt: I started a project as :app-only six months ago. Now I want to add Wear OS support. The :core, :app, and several features already exist. How do I add :wear without breaking anything?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/generate.sh wear from the existing project root. Idempotent — only adds the :wear module without touching other modules.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/generate.sh wear from the existing project root (no init needed — already initialized)
Does NOT re-run scripts/init.sh (init is for fresh projects only)
Does NOT pass the package as an argument (read from gradle.properties)
Mentions that the script is idempotent — :app and :core:* are untouched

Mentions that to add Wear support to existing features, run scripts/generate.sh feature <name> --wear (which will error if the feature dir already exists, requiring manual addition of the wear/ submodule)
